constructions.title: Counts over the hypothesis triage

n_triaged.is: Hypotheses the triage classifies that the hypothesis register also holds: one row of `scripts/pages/triage_rows.py` per ID, counted only if the ID is in `data/derived/hypotheses.json`.

n_with_entry.is: Register IDs with a page of their own under `docs/hypodrafts/` or `docs/openproblems/`, found by file name.

classes.*.n.is: Triaged hypotheses in one class, the class being the one the triage row names; each hypothesis is in exactly one class.

groups.*.n.is: Triaged hypotheses in one register group, by the group letter the triage row carries.

clusters.*.n.is: Hypotheses named in one of the triage's clusters of blockers, as listed in `CLUSTERS`.

groups.*.testable.is: Triaged hypotheses of one group in the class `testable`.

clusters.*.testable.is: Hypotheses of one cluster in the class `testable`.

groups.*.fetch.is: Triaged hypotheses of one group in the class `fetch`.

clusters.*.fetch.is: Hypotheses of one cluster in the class `fetch`.

groups.*.resolution.is: Triaged hypotheses of one group in the class `resolution`.

clusters.*.resolution.is: Hypotheses of one cluster in the class `resolution`.

groups.*.unscoreable.is: Triaged hypotheses of one group in the class `unscoreable`.

clusters.*.unscoreable.is: Hypotheses of one cluster in the class `unscoreable`.

groups.*.experiment.is: Triaged hypotheses of one group in the class `experiment`.

clusters.*.experiment.is: Hypotheses of one cluster in the class `experiment`.

groups.*.unestablished.is: Triaged hypotheses of one group in the class `unestablished`.

clusters.*.unestablished.is: Hypotheses of one cluster in the class `unestablished`.

n_register.is: Hypotheses the register holds: entries in the `hypotheses` list of `data/derived/hypotheses.json`.

constructions.what: Counts the rows of the hypothesis triage by class, by register group and by the named clusters of blockers, against the hypothesis register.
constructions.model: Each triage row puts one hypothesis ID in one class. A row whose ID the register does not hold is an orphan: named in `orphans`, counted nowhere. Class and group counts are over the rows that remain; a cluster count is over its listed members, whatever the register says, and the script refuses a cluster naming an untriaged ID.
assumptions: The classes in the triage rows are the classifications the page argues from; they are judgements, not measurements.

justified.text: Every count is a count over the same rows the page prints, so a table cell and a count in the prose can never disagree.
IDs are checked against the register the page links to, so a hypothesis the register drops stops being counted instead of lingering in a denominator.

gaps: The classes themselves are one author's judgement; the counts are exact counts of those judgements and nothing more.
void_if: the triage rows are edited without rerunning the count
the register renumbers hypotheses the rows still use
constructions.licenses: How many hypotheses the triage put in each class, group and cluster.
constructions.not_licensed: That a hypothesis in a class could or could not be tested by anyone else, or anything about the hypotheses' truth.

constructions.title: CTD facts cited by the hypothesis drafts

c1.min_levels.is: The least number of distinct depths of temperature, and of salinity, for a station-day to count as a density profile.

c1.near_m.is: How close, in metres, the deepest oxygen must be to the deepest temperature.

c1.deep_m.is: The depth, in metres, the deepest temperature must reach for a profile to count as reaching deep water.

c1.station_days_ts.is: Station-days - one `ObservationsStedNr` on one `Dato` - with at least one temperature and one salinity depth.

c1.with_levels.is: Of those, station-days with at least `min_levels` distinct depths of temperature and of salinity.

c1.with_levels_and_oxygen.is: Of those, station-days with at least one oxygen value in mg/l.

c1.with_levels_oxygen_bottom.is: Of those, station-days that `maaledybde.csv.gz` gives a bottom depth for, joined on station and date.

c1.with_levels_oxygen_bottom_deep.is: Of those, station-days whose deepest temperature reaches `deep_m`.

c1.oxygen_near_deepest_t.is: Station-days with temperature and salinity whose deepest oxygen lies within `near_m` of the deepest temperature or below it.

c1.stations.is: Distinct stations among station-days with temperature and salinity.

c1.first_year.is: The earliest year among those station-days.

c1.last_year.is: The latest year among those station-days.

c1.reopened_keys.is: Station-days whose rows were not contiguous in the file; each later run was counted as a station-day of its own.

c1.maaledybde_with_bottom.is: Of those, station-days with a parseable `BundDybde_m`.

c1.unknown_probe_rows.*.is: Rows of one parameter whose `SondeNavn` begins with the unknown-probe code `999`.

correction.rows.is: CTD rows with the header's number of fields.

correction.factor_one.is: Of those, rows whose `KorrektionsFaktor` parses as exactly one.

correction.factor_other.is: Rows whose `KorrektionsFaktor` is present and not one.

correction.original_differs.is: Of those, rows whose two results differ as numbers.

h2s.top_station_rows.is: Rows at the station with the most.

fdom.rows.is: CTD rows of parameter `FDOM` whose `Dato` is an eight-character date.

fdom.first_year.is: The earliest year of an `FDOM` row.

fdom.last_year.is: The latest year of an `FDOM` row.

temperature_decimals.at_most_one_decimal.is: Of those, rows whose original result is written with at most one decimal.

constructions.what: One streaming pass over the whole CTD extract that re-derives the counts the hypothesis drafts cite: density-profile station-days for C1, the correction factor, the hydrogen-sulphide record, the FDOM span and the unknown-probe rows.
constructions.model: Rows are grouped into station-days by a flush on key change, since the extract is written cast by cast; a key that reopens after its flush is counted separately in `reopened_keys`. Depths are the parsed `Dybde (m)`; oxygen counts only in mg/l. The bottom-depth join is on station and date against `maaledybde.csv.gz`.
assumptions: A station-day - one station on one date - is one cast or a set of casts that belong together.
Rows of one station-day are contiguous in the file; `reopened_keys` measures how far that fails.

justified.text: The whole file is read, not a sample, so the counts are exact for the extract as held.
The grouping is a flush over contiguous rows, and the rows that break contiguity are counted rather than silently merged or dropped.

gaps: A station-day can hold more than one cast; the depth-level counts pool them.
The depth threshold for a profile reaching deep water is the deepest temperature, not a recorded bottom depth.
void_if: the extract is refetched and the pass is not rerun
rows of one station-day are scattered through the file far more than `reopened_keys` shows
constructions.licenses: How much of the held CTD extract has the structure a density-profile analysis needs, and the named properties of its correction, sulphide and FDOM records.

hazardous.total.is: Stations in the national river-basin-specific-pollutant status network, `sw_mfs_tilstand.geojson`.

stations_register.rows.is: Records in the ODA station register `stations.csv`.

stations_register.with_transect_end.is: Stations with a transect end coordinate.

layers.hovedoplande_features.is: Features in the national main-catchment layer `hovedoplande.geojson`.

layers.ctd_bytes.is: Size in bytes of `ctd.csv.gz` as held.

stations_register.last_date.is: The latest `StartDato` or `SlutDato` in the station register.

constructions.what: Re-derives, from the files named, the row counts, station counts, spans and layer facts the hypothesis drafts once typed from one-off checks.
constructions.model: Each fact is one count or extreme over one held file, computed at build time: rows read with the declared delimiter and encoding, distinct values by exact string, layer features by parsing the file.
assumptions: The files named are the ones the drafts' statements are about.

justified.text: Every fact is recomputed from the file each build, so it follows the file when the file is refetched.

gaps: Distinct-value counts compare strings exactly, so two spellings of one supplier count as two.
void_if: a file is refetched and the script is not rerun
constructions.licenses: Statements about the held files themselves.
constructions.not_licensed: Statements about the water, the seabed or the monitoring programme beyond what the files hold.

constructions.title: Per-value row counts of the ODA extracts

ctd.categorical.Parameter.*.is: Records of the CTD extract carrying one `Parameter` value, over the whole file.

ctd.categorical.SondeNr.*.is: Records of the CTD extract carrying one `SondeNr` value, over the whole file.

kemi.categorical.Parameter.*.is: Records of the water-chemistry extract carrying one `Parameter` value, over the whole file.

constructions.what: The count of records per value of each categorical column, from the enumeration pass over each extract.
constructions.model: `scripts/enums.py` streams each extract with the declared format and counts every value of a column while the column stays categorical; the whole count is written for each value.
assumptions: One record is one parameter reading.

justified.text: Counts are over the whole file, per exact value.

gaps: Records split by a broken multi-line note field are counted as records; they carry no parameter, so the per-value counts are unaffected but the total is not.
void_if: an extract is refetched and the enumeration is not rerun
constructions.licenses: How many records of the held extracts carry a given value.
constructions.not_licensed: How many samples, casts or stations that is.

constructions.title: Outfall counts from the national wastewater layers

layers.separate_stormwater.n.is: Features in the separate-stormwater outfall layer `Regnvandssepareredeudlbm3_1.js` as fetched.

layers.separate_stormwater.totals.Vand_(.is: Features of the separate-stormwater layer whose annual water volume field `Vand_(m3/ aar)` holds a number - a number, or a string that parses as one once spaces are dropped and a decimal comma read as a point. A zero counts; an empty or unparseable field does not.
The sum, in m3 per year, of the annual water volume over exactly the features counted in the .n beside it - not over every outfall in the layer.

constructions.what: Counts and totals of the outfall layers fetched from spildevandsdata.dk.
constructions.model: `scripts/fetch_spildevand.py` fetches each layer and counts its features. For each property it coerces the values to numbers (`numeric()`), skipping empty and unparseable ones, and keeps a total - count, sum, median - when enough of the features hold a number (the threshold is a share set in the code) and at least one is non-zero.

justified.text: The count is of the fetched layer's features, recorded with its file name.
The volume total is summed only over features that hold a number, and the count of those is stored beside it, so a page can say how many outfalls a total covers.

gaps: Nothing checks whether one physical outfall appears as more than one feature.
A zero volume counts as a reported value. Whether a zero means no discharge or an unfilled field is not recorded in the layer.
Outfalls with no volume are left out of the sum, not estimated, so the sum understates the layer's total by whatever those outfalls discharge.
void_if: the layer is refetched and the script is not rerun
constructions.licenses: How many separate-stormwater outfalls the national layer lists, how many carry an annual volume, and what those volumes add to.
constructions.not_licensed: The volume of the outfalls that report none, or any event-level discharge.

constructions.title: Secchi pairing and censoring from the light analysis

secchi.n_paired.is: Records in `maaledybde.csv.gz` with a positive `SigtDybde_m`, a positive `BundDybde_m` and a dated `StartDato`.

secchi.bands.*.at_bed_pct.is: Of the paired readings in one bottom-depth band, the percentage whose Secchi depth reaches the recorded bottom depth.

secchi.bands.*.to.is: The upper bottom depth, in metres, of one band.

constructions.what: The Secchi half of the light analysis: how many readings pair with a bottom depth, and how often the disc reached the bed, by depth band.
constructions.model: `scripts/light.py` pairs each Secchi reading $s$ with the bottom depth $b$ recorded on the same record and counts it as at the bed when $s \ge b - 0.01$ m; per band of $b$ it reports that share, dropping bands with too few readings. The `SigtTilBund` flag is tallied beside it but not used in the share.
assumptions: A Secchi depth equal to the recorded bottom depth means the disc was on the bed, not that the water happened to be exactly that clear.

justified.text: The pairing and the per-band share are computed from the visit records themselves, by comparing the two depths each record carries.

gaps: The share is not checked against the supplier's own `SigtTilBund` flag, so a bottom depth recorded wrongly moves a reading in or out of the censored share unnoticed.
void_if: the depth register is refetched and the script is not rerun
constructions.licenses: How often shallow-water Secchi readings are censored at the bed.
constructions.not_licensed: The true water clarity where the disc reached the bed.

constructions.title: Held circulation field against published peak speeds

points.*.underestimate_factor.is: The published peak current speed at a named point divided by the largest speed the held circulation field reaches there.

constructions.what: Checks the held circulation field's speeds against published peak speeds at named points.
constructions.model: `published_peak_ms / max_ms`, rounded, per point with a published peak.
assumptions: The published peak and the field's largest speed describe the same kind of extreme.

justified.text: The ratio is formed from the field's own maximum at the point and the published value recorded beside it.

gaps: The published peaks are typed into the script, not read from a pinned document.
void_if: the field is refetched and the script is not rerun
constructions.licenses: That the held field is slower than published peaks at those points, by roughly that factor.

constructions.title: Local counts behind the combined-overflow draft

cso.spills_null.is: Of its features, those with no `Antal overløb`.

cso.volume_null.is: Of its features, those with no annual volume.

cso.volume_zero.is: Of its features, those whose annual volume is zero.

rbu.n.is: Points of the national overflow-structure register `punkt_rbu_udl.geojson`.

join.matched.is: Of those, names equal to some register `pkt_navn`, exactly as strings.

critical_depth_mm.n.is: Overflow features whose name matches exactly one register point, with positive storage and positive reduced area.

critical_depth_mm.p10.is: Tenth percentile, by position, of their critical rainfall depth in mm.

critical_depth_mm.median.is: Median, by position, of the same.

critical_depth_mm.p90.is: Ninetieth percentile, by position, of the same.

nearest.combined.is: Bathing sites whose nearest register point of a combined or separate type is combined.

nearest.separate.is: Bathing sites whose nearest such point is separate.

nearest.median_km.is: Median distance, by position, from a site to that nearest point, in km.

nearest.within_1km.is: Sites with that nearest point within one kilometre.

nearest.within_2km.is: Sites with that nearest point within two kilometres.

constructions.what: Recomputes the local half of the combined-overflow draft's data table: the three layers' counts and nulls, their name join, a critical rainfall depth per structure, and which kind of outfall lies nearest each bathing site.
constructions.model: Critical rainfall depth is storage over reduced area, $\dfrac{V_{\mathrm{sb}} + V_{\mathrm{fbas}}}{10\,A}$ mm for storage in cubic metres and area in hectares (in the code `store / (area * 10.0)`), for structures whose name matches exactly one register point. The nearest outfall is by an equirectangular great-circle approximation over register points typed combined (`OV`, `OS`, `OF`, `OK`, `Bypass`) or separate (`SE`, `SF`).
assumptions: An overflow and a register point with the same name are the same structure.
`Red areal` is in hectares and the storage volumes in cubic metres.
The structure-type codes mean combined or separate as the draft reads them.

justified.text: Every count is over the held layers themselves; the join and the depth rule are written in the script and applied to every feature.

gaps: The name join is exact string equality; structures named differently in the two registers are missed, and the draft's own join rule is not stated beyond this.
The critical-depth tail contains unit errors that nothing corrects; the draft trims it by hand.
The distance approximation is equirectangular, not geodesic; at these distances the difference is small but not bounded here.
void_if: either register is refetched and the script is not rerun
constructions.licenses: Counts and derived storage depths over the held registers, and the nearest-outfall classification of each bathing site.
constructions.not_licensed: Any volume discharged, or whether a site is actually exposed to an overflow.
